title: AxiomProver Autonomously Proves Fel’s Syzygy and Chen–Gendron k-Differential Conjectures in Lean 4
whyItMatters: AxiomProver’s debut breakthrough: autonomously discovered and Lean 4/Mathlib-verified proofs of both Fel’s Conjecture on numerical semigroup syzygies and the Chen–Gendron Conjecture on spin parity of k-differentials.
summary: Axiom Math researchers (with Ken Ono, Evan Chen, Dawei Chen, Kenny Lau, Jujian Zhang, Letong Hong, and collaborators) demonstrated AxiomProver’s first pair of genuine autonomous open-conjecture proofs directly from natural-language problem statements. AxiomProver proved Fel’s Conjecture on alternating syzygy power sums of numerical semigroups via exponential generating functions (arXiv:2602.03716, fully formalized in Lean/Mathlib) and solved the Chen–Gendron Conjecture A.10 determining spin parity of k-differentials in genus 0 and 1 overnight via an unexpected Jacobi-symbol reduction (arXiv:2602.03722, formalized in Lean/Mathlib). Both preprints underwent referee revisions in June–July 2026.
technicalHighlights: Autonomously proved Fel’s Conjecture on numerical semigroup syzygies from a natural-language statement and formalized the full proof in Lean/Mathlib (github.com/AxiomMath/fel-polynomial).
Solved the Chen–Gendron Conjecture on spin parity of k-differentials in genus 0 and 1 overnight via a novel Jacobi-symbol reformulation (github.com/AxiomMath/parity-differential).
Both papers were revised to address journal referee reports (June–July 2026), laying the foundation for AxiomProver’s later bounded prime gaps and CFSG breakthroughs.
caveats: Note that a separate third AxiomProver paper from the same February 2026 wave (arXiv:2602.05095 on dead ends in square-free walks) was later found to have been proved by Mirsky in 1947 and is deliberately excluded from this entry.

scoreRationale.foundational: Autonomously resolved two genuinely open research conjectures in commutative algebra and moduli of Riemann surfaces.
scoreRationale.ripple: Launched AxiomProver’s trajectory toward lowering bounded prime gaps to 212 and formalizing the 43.1M-line CFSG.
scoreRationale.verification: Both proofs are formalized in Lean 4 / Mathlib on public GitHub and have already passed referee-report revisions.
scoreRationale.velocity: Produced complete novel proofs and Lean formalizations overnight directly from natural-language statements.
